bug_semantics: bgp_flowspec_op_decode() in bgpd/bgp_flowspec_util.c walks a chained FlowSpec numeric-operator NLRI and, on BGP_FLOWSPEC_CONVERT_TO_NON_OPAQUE, writes each decoded operator into a caller-supplied struct bgp_pbr_match_val array sized BGP_PBR_MATCH_VAL_MAX (5) via mval++. The loop guard was `if (loop > BGP_PBR_MATCH_VAL_MAX) *error = -2` and the write path only skipped when *error == -2, so loop==5 still wrote mval[5] — one element past the end. A crafted FlowSpec component with more than five chained operators therefore caused a CWE-787 off-by-one out-of-bounds write (DoS). bgp_flowspec_bitmask_decode() used the same `>` comparison against the same 5-slot arrays.
flaw_origin: 47555ee921fadc4910eebce156ea773da8d46324 (Philippe Guibert, 2018-03-08) first implemented FlowSpec-to-PBR conversion: it added the `loop > BGP_PBR_MATCH_VAL_MAX` bound, the CONVERT_TO_NON_OPAQUE mval++ writes, and bgp_flowspec_match_rules_fill() callers that pass protocol/port/icmp/packet_length/dscp arrays of length 5. The parent commit still had CONVERT_TO_NON_OPAQUE as a TODO stub with no bound and no mval write. Later edits (2023 early-return braces in bitmask_decode; 2026 max_len guards) did not rewrite the `>` comparison in op_decode; git log -S and blame at the fix parent still attribute those lines to 47555ee.
